- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 5-day high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong mean-reversion signals (e.g., alternating +/– 0.5+ over 3 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; apply 1–3% downward correction for days 1–7, then revert to baseline after day 8.  
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.0–0.3) over 5+ days, model tends to drift; apply 1–2% downward correction for next 5–10 days to avoid false momentum.
